To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we detect solar-like oscillations and determine the global asteroseismic properties for 642 F-, G- - and K-type main sequence and subgiant Kepler stars, that we compare the relative number of oscillators with stellar properties from the Kepler Input catalogue, and that we compare the global asteroseisic parameters obtained using nine independent methods.
we have detected and characterized the global asteroseismic properties in 642 solar-like oscillating stars observed by Kepler.
we have detected oscillations in 42 per cent of stars in a large sample of main-sequence F- and G-type stars observed by Kepler.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the analysis of solar-like oscillators in a large sample of stars, the determination of their global asteroseismic properties, the comparison of complementary analysis techniques and the validation of the results.

the following topics: (1) the detection of solar-like oscillators in a large sample of stars; (2) the determination of global asteroseismic properties; (3) the validation of the results and the assessment of their reproducibility; (4) the analysis of the power-law relations; and (5) the analysis of correlations between the global asteroseismic quantities and stellar parameters from the KIC.

the following: (1) the validation of the asteroseismic results obtained from Kepler photometric observations; (2) the determination of the relative precision with which the parameters can, in principle, be measured; and (3) the identification of systematic effects that can influence the asteroseismic parameters derived from the analysis of solar-like oscillators.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the global asteroseismic properties are well defined and robust for the majority of the stars analysed in the sample.
the results are consistent with those of the previous studies of solar-like oscillators.
the asteroseismic properties for solar-like oscillations for the Kepler sample are consistent with the predictions from the theory of stellar oscillations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have detected solar-like oscillations for 642 main-sequence and red giant stars observed by Kepler, and we have shown the importance of using multiple complementary methods to derive the global asteroseismic properties.
there is a general consistency among the methods and that there are some differences in detail, which can be explained by the different analysis methods used.
the global asteroseismic properties for the solar-like oscillators presented here are robust and reliable, and that these results can be used for a wide range of scientific studies.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the global asteroseismic properties are robust and reproducible.
the asteroseismic parameters derived from the different methods are in good agreement, with relative differences between the methods of less than 2.5 per cent.

the relative precision of the global asteroseismic parameter measurements can be improved by a factor of two to four, which will have a significant impact on the accuracy of stellar ages and masses derived from the analysis of the oscillation frequencies.
